protocol.name: meter-first full-store rho, 1024 workers declared, depth 6, evicting dict
protocol.abort: K_STALL=32 consecutive squarings, armed by a guard admission

census_fidelity.dict: shipped dict28.o (evicting), twelve-word nodes, 128-bit slot-keyed, 4-probe chains
census_fidelity.why: trail >= guard ring (6) is required for guard stationarity; only the partition series at fixed S carries the W-dependence

capacity_spec.rule: buckets = next_pow2(2 x records to retain); capacity = 4 x buckets
capacity_spec.sizing_basis: MEASURED peak live occupancy of the shipped store (evidence/probe31.json), scaled from 8 measured workers to 1024 declared workers; the store is an evicting structure, so it holds the working set, not the arrivals
capacity_spec.instantiable: buckets = 2^19 and capacity = 2^21 are both held in uint64_t; the 2^128 figure in v30 was the ADDRESS SPACE (127-bit slot labels), not the bucket count, and the ledger no longer conflates them
capacity_spec.v30_flaw: buckets = 2^128 with dict28_ws_init(u64) and d28_ws.nb u64: the declared table could not exist. The address width (127-bit labels in a two-word ref) is unchanged and is exercised by the wide-access counters.
capacity_spec.loss_interaction: retrieval loss and eviction loss are the SAME counter: a record is unreachable exactly when its chain position exceeds PROBES, and the shipped insert evicts the chain tail at that point (d28_ws_deep = 0 in every fixture)

type_table.code_type: uint64_t (chain length <= PROBES enforced by eviction)

claim.rule: minimal n with 20000*2^(n/10000) >= W; checked EXACTLY as 20000^10000 * 2^n >= W^10000

rounding.rule: every row is an exact integer CEIL of its rational product: ceil(n*num/den) = -((-n*num)//den). The claim rounds UP (smallest n that covers W), so both the per-row cost and the score err on the safe side; v30 used steps*int(STEP), which truncated 0.8706 Ir/step.
rounding.v30_effect: steps*int(STEP) = steps*47903 under-charged by 0.8706 x 9.58e34 = 8.34e34 Ir

prices.source: evidence/exec31.json (gcov executed counts on the shipped scripts/ir28/dict28.c)
prices.why: protocol28.py calls state_key48w, dict28_slot_export, dict28_wide_lookup and dict28_wide_insert on the success path; the ledger prices exactly those symbols. The dense dict28_lookup/dict28_insert are retained as a comparison row only.

derived_rows.basis: explicit upper-bound derivations stated as such (12 lanes x 4 Ir; 6 ring compares x 3 Ir + one fits() test); they are charged, not omitted

trap.relation: window length >= family length + 2 (the two slots the ring-6 guard lets repeat at the window boundary), so the >=14-multiplication families the verdict names are inside the tested windows instead of being structurally excluded
trap.short_families: lengths <= 6 contribute exactly zero (W(1)=0, no slot repeats inside ring 6)
trap.v30_flaw: observer windows of length 2..12 with the ring-6 guard force >=7 distinct slots and a singleton, so zero admissions was structural; v31 tests lengths 14..22 and reports the counts it actually sees

success.route: nonparametric percentile bootstrap of the recorded fixture outcomes
success.v30_flaw: 0.5762 was the 5th percentile of Beta(k+1,n-k+1) draws -- a MODEL quantile. v31 resamples the fixture indicators themselves (the empirical distribution of the 320 recorded outcomes); the Beta row is kept only as a labelled comparison.
success.independence: deleted as a claim: no 2^-256 pair-collision statement is made. The walk's collision argument is the per-walk Markov bound plus the union-existence form already accepted; disjoint RNG streams between windows are stated in the protocol (seed0 + worker id), not converted into an independence probability.
